transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I... I came in because my family made me, honestly. They keep waving these bank papers in my face, saying they prove nothing was taken. But I know. For over a year now, I've known they're hiding my money. They use all these little things to cover it up—like, suddenly there's a fundraiser at the church, or they're planning some trip, or there's a new bill they just *had* to pay. 

Speaking of trips, my sister went to Florida last month. She said she found a cheap flight, but I know how much those tickets cost. I went to Florida once, back when I was a teenager. We drove the whole way in this beat-up old station wagon. The AC was broken, and I remember we stopped at this diner in Georgia where the waitress had the brightest red hair I've ever seen. She gave me an extra slice of pie. It was cherry, I think. Or maybe strawberry? I can't eat strawberries anymore, they give me a rash. 

Anyway, I have to keep confronting them. I just have to. I won't stop until they tell the truth about what they're doing with my money.
Do you ever hear voices or sounds when no one else is around?

Voices? No, I don't hear anything like that. It's actually real quiet where I stay. Well, except for the neighbors sometimes. They play this loud music, sounds like heavy metal or something with all that screaming. I don't get how people can listen to that. I like country music, mostly. The older stuff, you know? Like Johnny Cash. 

My grandpa used to play Johnny Cash on his old record player. It had this big brass horn on it, like something out of an old movie. I used to try and stick my arm down in the horn when I was a kid to see where the sound came from, and I got my wrist stuck in it once. My grandma had to use butter to slide my hand out. It was real messy. We used a lot of real butter back then, not like that fake margarine stuff they sell at the store now in those plastic tubs. That stuff doesn't even melt right on toast. It just sits there all yellow and shiny. I bought a tub of it last week because it was on sale, but I ended up just throwing it in the trash.

```json
{"intent": "Assess for memory impairment and cognitive decline to differentiate dementia from delusional disorder and mood disorders.", "question": "Have you or your family noticed you

Have I noticed what? You trailed off there, Doc. But if you're asking about my memory, no, my memory's sharp. Too sharp, probably. I remember every single dollar they've taken, every little excuse they've made. 

Like that time they said they needed money for a new water heater. A water heater! I know for a fact the one in the basement is only five years old. It's a Rheem, I think. Or maybe a Bradford White. My uncle used to install those. He was a plumber for thirty years. Had this old Ford truck that smelled like pipe glue and stale coffee. We used to ride in the back of it during the summer. You can't do that anymore, the cops will pull you right over. 

I got pulled over once for a busted taillight. It wasn't even my fault, some kid backed into me at the grocery store. The Piggly Wiggly over on 4th Street. They have the best fried chicken in the deli there, but you have to get it before noon or it gets all dry under those heat lamps. I hate dry chicken. It's like eating sawdust. Speaking of sawdust, my brother tried to build a birdhouse last spring and got sawdust all over the patio. He didn't even sweep it up. Just left it there for the wind to blow around. Typical. Just like how they think they can sweep my money under the rug. But I won't let them. I remember everything.

```json
{"intent": "Assess for decreased need for sleep to evaluate for a manic episode (F31.2).", "question": "Have you found that you need

Need what? Less sleep? No, I don't think so. I sleep just fine, honestly. I usually go to bed around ten, right after the late news. The anchor on channel four, he has this really strange comb-over. It's like he thinks nobody can tell, but it just swoops right across his forehead. Reminds me of my third-grade teacher, Mr. Henderson. He had the exact same hair, and he always smelled like peppermints. 

He used to keep a jar of those red and white striped peppermints on his desk. The ones wrapped in clear plastic that gets all twisted at the ends. I tried to open one once and cut my finger on the wrapper. It bled a lot for a tiny cut. Paper cuts are the worst, aren't they? I got a terrible one last week opening a letter from the bank. That's how I know they're still messing with my accounts, sending me these statements that don't add up. But anyway, yeah, sleep isn't a problem for me. I get my eight hours.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical or neurological conditions?

Medical conditions? No, I don't have anything like that. I'm healthy as a horse, really. Though horses get sick too, I guess. My cousin had a horse once, a big brown one named Buster. He got some kind of stomach thing and the vet had to come out in the middle of the night. It was pouring rain, just buckets coming down. 

I hate driving in the rain, especially when the wipers start squeaking. Mine were squeaking so bad last week I had to go to the auto parts store to get new ones. The guy there didn't even know how to put them on right. He had these greasy hands and got smudges all over my windshield. I had to use half a bottle of Windex when I got home just to see out of it again. Windex always leaves those blue streaks though if you don't use a paper towel. I tried using newspaper once because someone told me it works better, but the ink just got all over my hands. It took three days for it to wash off completely. But yeah, no, no medical problems for me.
Do you ever feel like an outside force or another person is controlling your thoughts, body, or actions?

Controlling my thoughts? No, no, nobody's controlling my mind or my body. That sounds like something out of one of those sci-fi movies. My brother used to watch those all the time. The ones with the aliens and the tin foil hats. He had this whole collection of VHS tapes in his room, stacked all the way up to the ceiling. 

One time, the whole stack fell over in the middle of the night and sounded like an earthquake. I thought the house was falling down! We lived in this old farmhouse back then, the kind with the wraparound porch where the floorboards creaked every time you took a step. My mom used to sit out there and shell peas in the summer. She had this big metal bowl that would ring like a bell if you hit it with a spoon. I used to do that just to annoy her. She'd get so mad, but she never really yelled. Just gave me that look, you know? The one that meant you better stop right now. But no, nobody is controlling me. I'm the only one in charge of my own head.
Do you drink alcohol or use any recreational drugs?

Alcohol? Drugs? No, I don't touch any of that stuff. I can't even stand the smell of beer, honestly. My stepdad used to drink those tall cans of cheap beer, the ones with the mountains on them that are supposed to turn blue when they're cold. He'd leave the empty cans all over the front porch. We had this old stray cat that used to come around back then, a big orange tabby with half an ear missing. I think it got in a fight with a raccoon or something. 

Raccoons are so mean, you know? They get into the trash and just tear the bags to absolute shreds. I had to clean up chicken bones and coffee grounds all over the driveway last Tuesday because the garbage men wouldn't take it when it spilled. They just drove right past my house. That truck is so loud it shakes the front windows every time it goes by. I tried putting weather stripping around the frames to stop the rattling, but the sticky part kept peeling off. It was that cheap foam kind from the dollar store. You really get what you pay for with that stuff, the glue is basically useless. But yeah, no, I don't drink or do drugs at all.
Have you had any periods where you felt constantly down, sad, or depressed?

Down? Sad? No, I don't really get sad like that. I mean, I cry when I chop onions, but everybody does that, right? I bought this huge sack of yellow onions from the produce stand on the highway last week because I wanted to make stew. Beef stew with the carrots and potatoes. But the potatoes they had were all soft and had those little eyes growing out of them. 

I hate when potatoes get like that, they look like little alien bugs or something. I tried cutting them off with a paring knife, but the knife was so dull it just kind of mashed the potato. I need to get a knife sharpener. My grandpa used to have one of those long metal sticks he'd scrape his knives against before carving the Thanksgiving turkey. He always made a big show out of it, wearing this ridiculous apron that said "Kiss the Cook" in bright red letters. The letters started peeling off in the wash though, so eventually it just said "Kiss the C." My grandma tried to sew a patch over it, but her sewing machine kept jamming. It was one of those heavy old Singer machines, the black ones with the gold curly designs on the side. You had to use a foot pedal to make it go. It weighed an absolute ton, I have no idea how she moved it around. But anyway, no, I haven't been depressed or anything like that.
Do you ever see things that other people don't seem to see?

See things? Like... like ghosts or something? No, I don't see anything that isn't there. I mean, my eyesight isn't what it used to be, I'll admit that. I was trying to read the back of a soup can the other day, the chicken noodle kind with the little star-shaped pasta, and the letters were just a blur. 

Those star pastas are so much better than the regular noodles, they don't get all soggy and fall apart on your spoon. I bought a whole case of that soup when it was on sale at the grocery store. The wheels on the shopping cart were completely busted, though. It kept pulling to the left so hard I almost crashed into a huge display of canned baked beans. Can you imagine the mess if I knocked all those over? Baked beans everywhere. The floor there is always so shiny, they must wax it every single night. I slipped on a wet floor once at a bowling alley when I was a kid. I was wearing those ugly rental shoes, the ones that are half red and half blue. They always smell like disinfectant spray. The guy behind the counter sprayed them right in front of me, this giant cloud of aerosol that made me sneeze like five times in a row. My nose gets so sensitive to strong smells like that. It's like how I can't stand the smell of lavender, it just gives me an instant headache. But no, I don't see things other people don't see. Just regular stuff.

```json
{"intent": "Differentiate pervasive personality pattern (F60.0) from a circumscribed delusional disorder (F22) by assessing if distrust of others is a lifelong trait

Have I always felt this way? You mean, like, not trusting people? Well, I don't know if I'd say always. I mean, I used to trust my old mailman, Mr. Henderson. He was this sweet older guy who always carried dog treats in his pocket. Not that I had a dog, but he'd give them to the neighbor's golden retriever. That dog was so hyper, it would jump up and get muddy paw prints all over my clean jeans. 

I hate doing laundry, you know? The washing machine I have now makes this awful grinding noise during the spin cycle. It sounds like there are rocks in there. I called a repair guy, but he wanted to charge me a hundred dollars just to look at it. A hundred dollars! I could buy a whole new wardrobe at the thrift store for that much. I love going to thrift stores, you never know what you're going to find. Last week I found this beautiful vintage teapot, painted with little blue flowers. It reminded me of the wallpaper in my great-aunt's kitchen. She had this tiny little kitchen that always smelled like cinnamon and old paper. She used to bake snickerdoodles every Sunday. I tried making snickerdoodles once, but I accidentally used salt instead of sugar. They were completely ruined. I had to throw the whole batch out in the yard for the birds. But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right. I guess I've just learned you have to be careful with people, you know? You can't just trust everyone right off the bat.

```json
{"intent": "Assess for functional impairment or decline in daily functioning outside the delusional belief to differentiate delusional disorder from schizophrenia.", "question": "Outside of the issues with your family and

Outside of all that? I mean, other than the arguments about the money, everything is pretty much the same. I still handle my own meals, get myself to the county clinic and my assistance appointments. I keep my things in order exactly the same way I always have. I'm very particular about my things. Like my canned goods, I have them all lined up by size and then by color of the label. 

The green labels have to go on the left. I bought these green beans once, the french-cut kind, but the can was dented. I didn't notice until I got home. Dented cans are so dangerous, you know, they can give you botulism. I saw a documentary about that on public television once. It was late at night, I couldn't sleep because the stray cats outside were yowling so loud. There's this one orange tabby that just sits on the fence and screams. I tried throwing a shoe at him once, just to scare him off, not to hit him. But it was one of my good fuzzy slippers and it got stuck in the rhododendron bush. 

Those bushes get so big if you don't trim them. My uncle had one that practically swallowed his whole front porch. He was always out there with these giant rusty clippers, hacking away at it. He wore these thick leather gloves that smelled like old grease. He worked at a garage, fixing transmissions all day. My transmission is acting up, actually. It slips when I try to go uphill. But anyway, yeah, I still do everything I need to do. I take care of myself just fine.

```json
{"intent": "Assess for tactile or somatic hallucinations to rule out somatic delusion or Criterion A for schizophrenia.", "question": "Have you ever felt unusual sensations on your skin or inside your body

Unusual sensations? No, I don't think so. I mean, sometimes my skin gets a little dry in the winter, especially on my elbows. I bought this lotion that was supposed to be extra moisturizing, it had cocoa butter in it. It smelled just like chocolate. I love chocolate, but I can't eat the kind with almonds because they get stuck in my teeth. 

I went to the dentist a few years ago and he used this horrible scraping tool. The sound it made against my teeth was like fingernails on a chalkboard. I hate that sound. It's like when someone drags a metal chair across a tile floor. They used to do that all the time in the cafeteria at my old school. The chairs had these rubber caps on the bottom, but they always fell off. We used to collect them and try to bounce them like little rubber balls, but they didn't really bounce. They just kind of thudded on the ground. 

My brother had a real rubber ball, one of those super bouncy ones, and he threw it right through the living room window once. My mom was so mad, she made him pay for it out of his allowance. It took him like six months to pay it off because he only got two dollars a week. Two dollars doesn't buy much these days, does it? You can barely get a candy bar for that. But no, I don't feel anything weird inside my body or on my skin. Just regular dry elbows sometimes.

```json
{"intent": "Assess for ideas or delusions of reference to further evaluate Criterion A for schizophrenia versus delusional disorder.", "question": "Do you ever feel like things on the television,

Like the TV is talking to me or something? No, I mean, the TV is just the TV. Although, I do watch a lot of game shows in the afternoon. I like the one where they have to guess the price of things, you know? But sometimes they pick the most ridiculous items. Like last week, they had this fancy espresso machine that cost over a thousand dollars. Who pays a thousand dollars for coffee? 

I just use instant coffee. It's so much easier. You just boil water and stir it in. My kettle has a little whistle on it when it's ready, but the whistle is broken now, so it just makes this sad, wheezing sound. It sounds exactly like my neighbor's pug. That dog is so overweight, it can barely walk down the driveway. They feed it table scraps all the time. I saw them giving it a whole piece of pepperoni pizza once. Pepperoni gives me such bad heartburn. I have to chew those little pink tablets if I even look at spicy food. 

They taste like chalk, though. Remember when teachers used to use real chalk on the blackboards? And they'd ask you to take the erasers outside and clap them together to get the dust out? I used to love doing that. The dust would fly everywhere like a little white cloud. It got all over my favorite blue sweater once, the one with the little pearl buttons. I lost one of those buttons at the grocery store and never found it. So I just had to wear it with a missing button for years. But no, the television doesn't say anything special to me. Just regular shows and commercials for things I can't afford.

```json
{"intent": "Assess for negative symptoms such as avolition or loss of motivation to rule out schizophrenia.", "question": "Have you experienced a loss of motivation

Loss of motivation? No, I don't think so. I still get up every day and do what I need to do. I have my routine, you know? Like making my instant coffee and lining up my canned goods. You have to stay on top of things like that, otherwise the pantry just becomes a disaster area. 

My sister's pantry is a complete mess. I was over there once, before all this trouble started, and she just had boxes of cereal shoved in sideways. And she buys that sugary stuff with the little marshmallows in it. I don't know how anyone can eat that for breakfast. It's like eating candy first thing in the morning. When we were kids, my mom would only let us have plain corn flakes or oatmeal. She'd make the oatmeal on the stove, not in the microwave like people do now. Microwaves make everything taste a little rubbery, don't you think? 

I tried to heat up a leftover piece of meatloaf in the microwave once, and it came out so tough I could barely cut it with a knife. It was one of those good steak knives, too, with the wooden handle. My dad bought a whole set of them from a door-to-door salesman when I was little. The salesman had this huge leather briefcase that smelled like shoe polish. He sat right at our kitchen table and demonstrated how sharp they were by cutting a penny in half. I still don't know how he did that. It must have been a trick penny or something. You can't just cut through solid copper like that. Or maybe pennies aren't even made of copper anymore. I heard they're mostly zinc now. Zinc is good for you, though, right? Like in those lozenges you take when you have a cold. I hate the cherry flavored ones, they taste like cough syrup. But anyway, yeah, I still have plenty of motivation to do my daily chores and everything.

```json
{"intent": "Assess for olfactory or gustatory hallucinations to complete the evaluation of Criterion A for schizophrenia.", "question": "Have you ever smelled or tasted things that

Smelled or tasted things that aren't there? No, nothing like that. My sense of smell is pretty normal, I guess. I mean, I can always tell when the neighbors are having a barbecue. They use that really cheap lighter fluid, and it makes everything smell like gasoline for hours. I don't know why they don't just use one of those chimney starter things. My uncle had one of those. He was obsessed with grilling. He would grill in the middle of winter, standing out in the snow with a huge parka on. 

He had this parka that was bright orange, like a traffic cone. You could see him from a mile away. He wore it everywhere, even to the grocery store. He said it was because he wanted hunters to see him if he ever got lost in the woods, but he lived in the suburbs. There were no woods anywhere near his house. Just a bunch of strip malls and that one diner that was shaped like a train car. 

I loved going to that diner. They had the best milkshakes. They brought them to you in those tall metal cups, and there was always extra left over. I always got strawberry. Real strawberry, not the fake syrup kind. The fake syrup always tastes a little bit like plastic, doesn't it? Like if you left a plastic bottle in a hot car all day and then drank out of it. That happened to me once when I was driving cross-country with my friend Sarah. We broke down in the middle of nowhere in Nevada. It was so hot, I thought the tires were going to melt right onto the asphalt. We had to wait three hours for a tow truck. The guy who drove the tow truck was missing his front tooth and kept whistling every time he talked. But no, I don't smell or taste anything weird. Just the usual stuff.

```json
{"intent": "Assess for flat affect or diminished emotional expression to rule out negative symptoms of schizophrenia.", "question": "Have you or others noticed that you show less emotion or

Show less emotion? No, I don't think so. I mean, nobody's ever said anything like that to me. I still laugh when things are funny and get upset when things go wrong, you know? Like the other day, I was at the grocery store, and they completely rearranged the aisles. I was so frustrated! I just wanted to find the canned peaches. 

I always buy the ones in heavy syrup, not the juice. The juice just tastes watered down. My grandmother used to can her own peaches. She had this huge garden in her backyard, and she grew everything. Tomatoes, cucumbers, zucchini... She used to make this zucchini bread that was so moist and sweet. She'd put walnuts in it, too. I love walnuts, but they're so expensive now. A little bag of them is like eight dollars! 

I went to a farmer's market once, thinking it would be cheaper, but it was actually more expensive. They had all these artisanal things, like goat milk soap and homemade jams. I bought a jar of blackberry jam, and it had so many seeds in it, it was almost crunchy. I hate when jam is crunchy. It gets stuck in your teeth. I had a piece of popcorn stuck in my teeth for three days once. It drove me absolutely crazy. I kept trying to get it out with a toothpick, but I just pushed it in further. I ended up having to go to the dentist, and he charged me fifty dollars just to pull it out. Fifty dollars for one piece of popcorn! I could have bought a whole case of canned peaches with that. But yeah, no, my emotions are perfectly fine. I feel things just like I always have.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about medical or neurological conditions, which is not covered by any of my symptom profile items (Delusions, Additional Requirement 1, Functional Impairment, Duration).

patient.answer:
Medical conditions? No, I don't have anything like that. I'm healthy as a horse, really. Though horses get sick too, I guess. My cousin had a horse once, a big brown one named Buster. He got some kind of stomach thing and the vet had to come out in the middle of the night. It was pouring rain, just buckets coming down. 

I hate driving in the rain, especially when the wipers start squeaking. Mine were squeaking so bad last week I had to go to the auto parts store to get new ones. The guy there didn't even know how to put them on right. He had these greasy hands and got smudges all over my windshield. I had to use half a bottle of Windex when I got home just to see out of it again. Windex always leaves those blue streaks though if you don't use a paper towel. I tried using newspaper once because someone told me it works better, but the ink just got all over my hands. It took three days for it to wash off completely. But yeah, no, no medical problems for me.

inference.note: Ruled out F06.2 due to the absence of underlying medical or neurological conditions.

doctor.intent: Assess for delusions of control, influence, or passivity to differentiate paranoid schizophrenia (F20.0) from delusional disorder (F22).
doctor.question: Do you ever feel like an outside force or another person is controlling your thoughts, body, or actions?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about delusions of control (feeling like an outside force is controlling thoughts, body, or actions), which is a symptom of schizophrenia or other psychotic disorders. My symptom profile only includes non-bizarre delusions about family/friends hiding money (S019), and does not mention delusions of control.

patient.answer:
Controlling my thoughts? No, no, nobody's controlling my mind or my body. That sounds like something out of one of those sci-fi movies. My brother used to watch those all the time. The ones with the aliens and the tin foil hats. He had this whole collection of VHS tapes in his room, stacked all the way up to the ceiling. 

One time, the whole stack fell over in the middle of the night and sounded like an earthquake. I thought the house was falling down! We lived in this old farmhouse back then, the kind with the wraparound porch where the floorboards creaked every time you took a step. My mom used to sit out there and shell peas in the summer. She had this big metal bowl that would ring like a bell if you hit it with a spoon. I used to do that just to annoy her. She'd get so mad, but she never really yelled. Just gave me that look, you know? The one that meant you better stop right now. But no, nobody is controlling me. I'm the only one in charge of my own head.

doctor.intent: Assess for substance or alcohol use to rule out a substance-induced psychotic disorder.
doctor.question: Do you drink alcohol or use any recreational drugs?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about substance use (alcohol or recreational drugs), which is not covered by any of the items in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Alcohol? Drugs? No, I don't touch any of that stuff. I can't even stand the smell of beer, honestly. My stepdad used to drink those tall cans of cheap beer, the ones with the mountains on them that are supposed to turn blue when they're cold. He'd leave the empty cans all over the front porch. We had this old stray cat that used to come around back then, a big orange tabby with half an ear missing. I think it got in a fight with a raccoon or something. 

Raccoons are so mean, you know? They get into the trash and just tear the bags to absolute shreds. I had to clean up chicken bones and coffee grounds all over the driveway last Tuesday because the garbage men wouldn't take it when it spilled. They just drove right past my house. That truck is so loud it shakes the front windows every time it goes by. I tried putting weather stripping around the frames to stop the rattling, but the sticky part kept peeling off. It was that cheap foam kind from the dollar store. You really get what you pay for with that stuff, the glue is basically useless. But yeah, no, I don't drink or do drugs at all.

doctor.intent: Assess for a history of depressive symptoms to evaluate for schizoaffective disorder or mood disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: Have you had any periods where you felt constantly down, sad, or depressed?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about periods of feeling down, sad, or depressed (depressive symptoms). My symptom profile covers delusions, functional impairment, and duration, but does not include any information about mood symptoms like depression.

patient.answer:
Down? Sad? No, I don't really get sad like that. I mean, I cry when I chop onions, but everybody does that, right? I bought this huge sack of yellow onions from the produce stand on the highway last week because I wanted to make stew. Beef stew with the carrots and potatoes. But the potatoes they had were all soft and had those little eyes growing out of them. 

I hate when potatoes get like that, they look like little alien bugs or something. I tried cutting them off with a paring knife, but the knife was so dull it just kind of mashed the potato. I need to get a knife sharpener. My grandpa used to have one of those long metal sticks he'd scrape his knives against before carving the Thanksgiving turkey. He always made a big show out of it, wearing this ridiculous apron that said "Kiss the Cook" in bright red letters. The letters started peeling off in the wash though, so eventually it just said "Kiss the C." My grandma tried to sew a patch over it, but her sewing machine kept jamming. It was one of those heavy old Singer machines, the black ones with the gold curly designs on the side. You had to use a foot pedal to make it go. It weighed an absolute ton, I have no idea how she moved it around. But anyway, no, I haven't been depressed or anything like that.

doctor.intent: Assess for visual hallucinations to evaluate psychotic disorder criteria
doctor.question: Do you ever see things that other people don't seem to see?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about visual hallucinations (seeing things other people don't see). My symptom profile covers delusions, functioning, functional impairment, and duration, but does not include any information about hallucinations.

patient.answer:
See things? Like... like ghosts or something? No, I don't see anything that isn't there. I mean, my eyesight isn't what it used to be, I'll admit that. I was trying to read the back of a soup can the other day, the chicken noodle kind with the little star-shaped pasta, and the letters were just a blur. 

Those star pastas are so much better than the regular noodles, they don't get all soggy and fall apart on your spoon. I bought a whole case of that soup when it was on sale at the grocery store. The wheels on the shopping cart were completely busted, though. It kept pulling to the left so hard I almost crashed into a huge display of canned baked beans. Can you imagine the mess if I knocked all those over? Baked beans everywhere. The floor there is always so shiny, they must wax it every single night. I slipped on a wet floor once at a bowling alley when I was a kid. I was wearing those ugly rental shoes, the ones that are half red and half blue. They always smell like disinfectant spray. The guy behind the counter sprayed them right in front of me, this giant cloud of aerosol that made me sneeze like five times in a row. My nose gets so sensitive to strong smells like that. It's like how I can't stand the smell of lavender, it just gives me an instant headache. But no, I don't see things other people don't see. Just regular stuff.

inference.note: Initial candidates based on a persistent non-bizarre persecutory/theft delusion lasting over a year without prominent hallucinations, mood episodes, or substance use, presenting with highly circumstantial speech.

Outside of all that? I mean, other than the arguments about the money, everything is pretty much the same. I still handle my own meals, get myself to the county clinic and my assistance appointments. I keep my things in order exactly the same way I always have. I'm very particular about my things. Like my canned goods, I have them all lined up by size and then by color of the label. 

The green labels have to go on the left. I bought these green beans once, the french-cut kind, but the can was dented. I didn't notice until I got home. Dented cans are so dangerous, you know, they can give you botulism. I saw a documentary about that on public television once. It was late at night, I couldn't sleep because the stray cats outside were yowling so loud. There's this one orange tabby that just sits on the fence and screams. I tried throwing a shoe at him once, just to scare him off, not to hit him. But it was one of my good fuzzy slippers and it got stuck in the rhododendron bush. 

Those bushes get so big if you don't trim them. My uncle had one that practically swallowed his whole front porch. He was always out there with these giant rusty clippers, hacking away at it. He wore these thick leather gloves that smelled like old grease. He worked at a garage, fixing transmissions all day. My transmission is acting up, actually. It slips when I try to go uphill. But anyway, yeah, I still do everything I need to do. I take care of myself just fine.

patient.answer:
Unusual sensations? No, I don't think so. I mean, sometimes my skin gets a little dry in the winter, especially on my elbows. I bought this lotion that was supposed to be extra moisturizing, it had cocoa butter in it. It smelled just like chocolate. I love chocolate, but I can't eat the kind with almonds because they get stuck in my teeth. 

I went to the dentist a few years ago and he used this horrible scraping tool. The sound it made against my teeth was like fingernails on a chalkboard. I hate that sound. It's like when someone drags a metal chair across a tile floor. They used to do that all the time in the cafeteria at my old school. The chairs had these rubber caps on the bottom, but they always fell off. We used to collect them and try to bounce them like little rubber balls, but they didn't really bounce. They just kind of thudded on the ground. 

My brother had a real rubber ball, one of those super bouncy ones, and he threw it right through the living room window once. My mom was so mad, she made him pay for it out of his allowance. It took him like six months to pay it off because he only got two dollars a week. Two dollars doesn't buy much these days, does it? You can barely get a candy bar for that. But no, I don't feel anything weird inside my body or on my skin. Just regular dry elbows sometimes.

patient.answer:
Like the TV is talking to me or something? No, I mean, the TV is just the TV. Although, I do watch a lot of game shows in the afternoon. I like the one where they have to guess the price of things, you know? But sometimes they pick the most ridiculous items. Like last week, they had this fancy espresso machine that cost over a thousand dollars. Who pays a thousand dollars for coffee? 

I just use instant coffee. It's so much easier. You just boil water and stir it in. My kettle has a little whistle on it when it's ready, but the whistle is broken now, so it just makes this sad, wheezing sound. It sounds exactly like my neighbor's pug. That dog is so overweight, it can barely walk down the driveway. They feed it table scraps all the time. I saw them giving it a whole piece of pepperoni pizza once. Pepperoni gives me such bad heartburn. I have to chew those little pink tablets if I even look at spicy food. 

They taste like chalk, though. Remember when teachers used to use real chalk on the blackboards? And they'd ask you to take the erasers outside and clap them together to get the dust out? I used to love doing that. The dust would fly everywhere like a little white cloud. It got all over my favorite blue sweater once, the one with the little pearl buttons. I lost one of those buttons at the grocery store and never found it. So I just had to wear it with a missing button for years. But no, the television doesn't say anything special to me. Just regular shows and commercials for things I can't afford.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about negative symptoms (loss of motivation/avolition), which is not covered by my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Loss of motivation? No, I don't think so. I still get up every day and do what I need to do. I have my routine, you know? Like making my instant coffee and lining up my canned goods. You have to stay on top of things like that, otherwise the pantry just becomes a disaster area. 

My sister's pantry is a complete mess. I was over there once, before all this trouble started, and she just had boxes of cereal shoved in sideways. And she buys that sugary stuff with the little marshmallows in it. I don't know how anyone can eat that for breakfast. It's like eating candy first thing in the morning. When we were kids, my mom would only let us have plain corn flakes or oatmeal. She'd make the oatmeal on the stove, not in the microwave like people do now. Microwaves make everything taste a little rubbery, don't you think? 

I tried to heat up a leftover piece of meatloaf in the microwave once, and it came out so tough I could barely cut it with a knife. It was one of those good steak knives, too, with the wooden handle. My dad bought a whole set of them from a door-to-door salesman when I was little. The salesman had this huge leather briefcase that smelled like shoe polish. He sat right at our kitchen table and demonstrated how sharp they were by cutting a penny in half. I still don't know how he did that. It must have been a trick penny or something. You can't just cut through solid copper like that. Or maybe pennies aren't even made of copper anymore. I heard they're mostly zinc now. Zinc is good for you, though, right? Like in those lozenges you take when you have a cold. I hate the cherry flavored ones, they taste like cough syrup. But anyway, yeah, I still have plenty of motivation to do my daily chores and everything.

patient.answer:
Smelled or tasted things that aren't there? No, nothing like that. My sense of smell is pretty normal, I guess. I mean, I can always tell when the neighbors are having a barbecue. They use that really cheap lighter fluid, and it makes everything smell like gasoline for hours. I don't know why they don't just use one of those chimney starter things. My uncle had one of those. He was obsessed with grilling. He would grill in the middle of winter, standing out in the snow with a huge parka on. 

He had this parka that was bright orange, like a traffic cone. You could see him from a mile away. He wore it everywhere, even to the grocery store. He said it was because he wanted hunters to see him if he ever got lost in the woods, but he lived in the suburbs. There were no woods anywhere near his house. Just a bunch of strip malls and that one diner that was shaped like a train car. 

I loved going to that diner. They had the best milkshakes. They brought them to you in those tall metal cups, and there was always extra left over. I always got strawberry. Real strawberry, not the fake syrup kind. The fake syrup always tastes a little bit like plastic, doesn't it? Like if you left a plastic bottle in a hot car all day and then drank out of it. That happened to me once when I was driving cross-country with my friend Sarah. We broke down in the middle of nowhere in Nevada. It was so hot, I thought the tires were going to melt right onto the asphalt. We had to wait three hours for a tow truck. The guy who drove the tow truck was missing his front tooth and kept whistling every time he talked. But no, I don't smell or taste anything weird. Just the usual stuff.

Like the other day, I was at the grocery store, and they completely rearranged the aisles. I was so frustrated! I just wanted to find the canned peaches. 

I always buy the ones in heavy syrup, not the juice. The juice just tastes watered down. My grandmother used to can her own peaches. She had this huge garden in her backyard, and she grew everything. Tomatoes, cucumbers, zucchini... She used to make this zucchini bread that was so moist and sweet. She'd put walnuts in it, too. I love walnuts, but they're so expensive now. A little bag of them is like eight dollars! 

I went to a farmer's market once, thinking it would be cheaper, but it was actually more expensive. They had all these artisanal things, like goat milk soap and homemade jams. I bought a jar of blackberry jam, and it had so many seeds in it, it was almost crunchy. I hate when jam is crunchy. It gets stuck in your teeth. I had a piece of popcorn stuck in my teeth for three days once. It drove me absolutely crazy. I kept trying to get it out with a toothpick, but I just pushed it in further. I ended up having to go to the dentist, and he charged me fifty dollars just to pull it out. Fifty dollars for one piece of popcorn! I could have bought a whole case of canned peaches with that. But yeah, no, my emotions are perfectly fine. I feel things just like I always have.
